The main result was a stronger reduction of alcohol cue-induced activation in the ventral and dorsal striatum, the anterior cingulate cortex, the precentral gyrus, the insula, and several frontal areas in those alcohol-dependent patients who received CET in addition to standard clinical treatment compared with those who underwent standard clinical treatment only.

The final sample consisted of 15 patients in the CET group (9 male patients; age 50 ± 8 years, range 37–65 years) and 15 control patients (10 male patients; age 43 ± 9 years, range 27–57 years).

Data from five participants were excluded from analysis because of heavy movement in the scanner (> 3 mm in x, y, or z direction or > 3° rotation in any direction). Eight patients dropped out because of relapse during treatment (three CET group, five control group).
